It now draws a clean digit **0**: ```svg ``` **What changed:** - **It shows a zero:** a pill-shaped outline drawn from basic shapes, so it doesn't depend on any installed font. I guessed it should be a zero because of the filename. - **It scales properly:** the `viewBox` lets it resize without blurring, and `width`/`height` give it a default 24px size instead of the browser's 300×150 blank box. - **It matches common icon sets:** it uses the same 24×24 grid with a 2px line as libraries like Lucide and Feather. The edges line up with whole pixels, so it looks sharp at 24px. - **It takes on the text color:** `currentColor` means that when the code is pasted into a page, it uses the surrounding text color. When loaded as an ``, it's black. - **Screen readers can name it:** `role="img"` plus `` let them read it as "0". **Not verified visually:** the command to look for an image converter was blocked by the permission system, so I couldn't render it to an image and look at it. I checked the positions and sizes by hand instead. Open it in a browser for a quick look. To undo, the original file was exactly `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"/>`. If you meant it as a blank placeholder, or want a different look (solid shape, slashed zero, larger default size), tell me and I'll change it.
